name: Hephzibah
overview: Hephzibah is a female figure noted in Scripture primarily as the mother of King Manasseh of Judah. While her tribal affiliation and additional biographical details are not recorded, her role as a queen mother places her within the royal lineage of Judah. The biblical text provides limited information about her beyond this maternal connection.
namesAndTitles: The name Hephzibah means 'my pleasure is in her,' reflecting a positive and affectionate meaning. This proper name is recorded in 2 Kings 21:1 and is not indicated as being given by God. The name itself does not carry a specific prophetic or theological title but denotes a personal identity within the biblical narrative.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture explicitly identifies Hephzibah as the mother of Manasseh, who became king of Judah. No other family relationships are documented in the biblical record beyond this maternal link. Thus, her familial significance is centered on her son, King Manasseh.
scriptureSignificance: Hephzibah's significance in the biblical narrative is primarily tied to her position as the mother of King Manasseh, one of Judah's longest-reigning kings. Though the text does not elaborate on her personal actions or character, her role as queen mother situates her within the royal household during a critical period in Judah's history. Her mention underscores the importance of lineage and maternal influence in the Davidic monarchy.
